title: I Just Bought $10,000 Of This Stock
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Joseph Carlson executes a pre-set buy: two months ago he set a $10,000 buy-in price for every stock in his portfolio, and Netflix was the first to hit its trigger, falling to $60 - down roughly 50% from its all-time highs. He adds $10,000 to his Netflix position at $60, arguing the engagement scare is misread: YouTube watch time counts music and ambient listening, Netflix is event-driven television, and churn actually fell year over year. At 16x next-twelve-months earnings he calls the valuation attractive if the fundamentals hold, with the bear case being real engagement deterioration. He then walks through his whole $1.46m portfolio (191% time-weighted return vs ~170% for the S&P 500, ~$500k in gains): Mastercard (continue to hold, ~$70k gains), Amazon (a more attractive buy today, expects it to become his largest holding), Meta (entered this year, down $17k, holding through the volatility, enthusiastic about Muse), Google (continue to hold, 19x forward P/E, Cloud growing), S&P Global, Microsoft, ASML (trimmed 20% near $1,900), Costco (holding, not adding since 2023), Texas Roadhouse (best-timed entry, cost $89 vs $191), Moody's, Duolingo (cost $193 vs $160, still likes the story), Uber and DoorDash (both held). He also answers criticism that he only talks about winners, reviewing past sales: Apple sold for a $35,500 gain (a mistake in hindsight), Salesforce and Intuit sold at losses as AI disintermediates their businesses, with proceeds rotated into Meta; total realized gains $76,000. The fail of the week is Leopold Aschenbrenner, whose new fund is down ~90% after levered AI bets collapsed again. Conditional buys restated: Google at $250 (now $277), Uber at $60, ASML at an unstated trigger.
